version.value: Monophonic Marian antiphon, performed by a solo singer
version.note: The Hildegard Society identifies the antiphon in the Dendermonde manuscript, not Ordo virtutum. The recording pages’ dramatic attribution and associated circa-1151 date are rejected. The performer’s edition is unknown.

date.note: Hildegard’s twelfth-century authorship is established; an exact composition year is not. The Society treats reasons for omission from the Riesencodex as possibilities, not facts.

completeness.value: Complete nominated antiphon performance with final applause removed
completeness.note: The derivative’s source note explicitly identifies applause removal. No musical abridgement is documented, and Contrapunctus makes no further cut.

mode.note: Beverly Lomer gives D mode, range A below the final to the D above, principally syllabic writing, neumatic elements and short melismas. These written pitches do not establish the performance’s absolute pitch or tuning.

performers.note: The creator says performed live by self. The original’s embedded author tag reads Magdalen Kadel; the public credit retains the explicitly licensed username rather than expanding the performer’s name from an embedded tag alone.

date.note: The edited file’s description states 2006 and live performance. The original was uploaded on 23 March 2006; that day is not promoted to a session date. The derivative was uploaded on 1 October 2008.

place.note: Neither file description names the venue or town.

label.note: No recording label is identified; the source is a creator-uploaded performance.

catalogue.note: No release catalogue number is given.

matrixTakeSides.note: The original session medium and any take identifier are not documented.

credits.value: Original performance upload by Makemi; applause-removed derivative uploaded by Adam Cuerden
credits.note: These are uploader and derivative-provenance credits. A separately named recording engineer is not established.

date.note: The 2008 derivative upload dates the deposited file, not necessarily the editing operation. No separate mastering date is known.

processing.value: Applause at the end removed from O frondens.ogg; Ogg Vorbis derivative and Wikimedia MP3 transcode
processing.note: The source explicitly describes this non-musical trim. The derivative names Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20040629. No other restoration, tuning correction or musical edit is established.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative of the applause-removed Ogg Vorbis file

composition.note: The Commons Composition block applies public-domain status to Hildegard’s work. It does not license the modern sound recording.

recording.value: Rule 1 — CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported, performer’s release
recording.note: The separately headed Performance block names Makemi as copyright holder and grants CC BY-SA 3.0 through GFDL migration; the original creator upload supplies the same licensing chain. audio.mjs selects the composition’s Public domain tag, so that automatic result is not used as recording clearance.

rights.creditLine: Hildegard of Bingen, O frondens virga, Marian antiphon; performed live by Makemi, 2006. Original recording released by Makemi; applause-removed derivative uploaded by Adam Cuerden, Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 3.0. No additional audio edit by Contrapunctus.

editorial.timing: audio.mjs analyze completed before annotation; cache/analysis/origins-hildegard-o-frondens.txt was read. The short continuous antiphon has one authored section; no invented internal joins. Three cues at 32-second intervals, two musical and one contextual, use the short-work exception.
editorial.orchestra: Omitted because this is one unaccompanied voice. D mode describes the manuscript, not a claim of sounding D or A=440.
